Mechanism CONFIRMED (AC1), and the fix is authored on branch `fix-caused-by-lagging-checkout`.

**Divergence point, cited.** `commit_impact.referencing_commits` ran
`git -C <repo_root> log --format=%H%x1f%B%x00` with **no rev argument**
(`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:186-192`, pre-fix), so it walked HEAD alone.
`caused_by_refusal` (`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:31`) passes
`_code_root(repo_root)` = `config.repo_root(None)`, which through MCP is
`REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` — cloned ONCE at container boot by
`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:290` and never checked out again. The snapshot machinery's
`fetch_origin` advances `refs/remotes/origin/main`; nothing advances HEAD.

**Reproduced (not inferred).** A `--single-branch` clone, one upstream commit subject
`d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231: async gate start (P2)`, then `git fetch` in the clone:
`git log` shows only the clone-time commit, `git log --all` shows both, and
`referencing_commits` returns `[]` in the clone against `['c67195b…']` in the up-to-date
checkout. Same ticket, same commit, two verdicts — the CLI/MCP split in one process.

**Independent corroboration.** `_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:328-338`
already forces every inbound link, with a comment naming this exact mechanism: "its evidence
(e.g. the introducing commit behind a caused_by) may live only in the peer's clone."

**Fix.** The scan gains an opt-in `include_upstream` that adds the remote-tracking refs for
the checkout's OWN branch. Deliberately NOT `--all`: rebar's default layout keeps the ticket
event log on a `tickets` branch of the SAME repository, so `--all` walks one commit per
ticket event — wrong history, unbounded volume. When that still finds nothing, the guard
only treats absence as PROVEN by a checkout that is the whole history: no remote qualifies
outright; a replica is refreshed once (bounded `git fetch` under the existing
`fetch_coordination_lock`) and rescanned; a refresh that cannot complete leaves absence
unestablished, which is the same epistemic position as an unreadable history and takes the
same answer — allow. The check is NOT skipped on MCP, and the refusal is unchanged for a
genuinely commit-less target in a complete checkout.

The close gate's scan keeps its exact argv (`include_upstream` is opt-in), so its
"reachable from your worktree's current HEAD" contract is untouched — pinned by a test.

**Tests (RED before GREEN).** Four new behavioural tests in
`tests/unit/test_caused_by_link_validation.py` all failed with the reported refusal text
before the fix and pass after; one of them drives the **MCP `link_tickets` tool** with
`REBAR_ROOT` pointed at the lagging checkout, so the defect's own entry point is proven
rather than the library's. A fifth pins the close gate's HEAD-scoped scan against widening.

Change 2704 (patch set 3) is double-green — `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, 0 unresolved, out of WIP,
submittable. Not submitted and not closing this ticket; both are the operator's.

Review round: PS2 took an `LLM-Review -1` for a real gap — every new test that configured a remote
ended in an ALLOW, so nothing pinned "remote present, refresh succeeded, target still genuinely
commitless -> REFUSE". Without that direction a regression that allowed everything after a refresh
would have passed. Added at both surfaces (library and MCP `link_tickets`).

Also taken on PS3: `_has_remote` became `_remote_probe`, a tri-state. Collapsing "the probe failed
or hung" onto "no remote configured" would have manufactured a refusal — and therefore a
`--force`-only dead end — out of a checkout fault, which is this bug's own failure mode wearing a
different cause. `unknown` is now indeterminate and allows, pinned by a test that makes `git remote`
raise `TimeoutExpired`. And `git_history_read_ms` is captured after the upstream-ref resolution so
the metric still names only the history read.

Local `make verify`: lint and typecheck clean; the test leg reported 14 failures, 13 of them
`GateCongestedError: all 4 concurrent slots busy` and one a `claude mcp list` subprocess timeout.
Three `make verify` runs from sibling sessions were executing on this host at the same time
(`fix-alias-resolve-scan`, `rebar-membound`, this worktree), all sharing the 4-slot gate semaphore.
None of the failures touch `link`, `caused_by` or `commit_impact`; CI's own `Verified +1` on the
same tree is green.

compiled_state.description:
## Observed

While attributing bug `ff4a-2832-def4-4e55`, `link_tickets(ff4a…, d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231, "caused_by")`
routed through the **MCP server** was refused:

```
Error: cannot create caused_by link — target ticket 'd80d-7be7-1c0a-4231' has no commit
referencing it, so it cannot be shown to have introduced anything.
```

The claim is false. Commit `44ec1c2e67373a2e2b888a1beb0bf1cb7b0f6d39` has the subject
`d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231: async gate start (P2)`. Running the identical `rebar link` from a local
worktree with full history **succeeded immediately**.

## Confirmed mechanism (reproduced 2026-09-05)

`caused_by_refusal` (`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:31`) calls
`commit_impact.referencing_commits({target}, tracker, code_root)`
(`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:166`), whose scan runs
`git -C <repo_root> log --format=%H%x1f%B%x00` — **no rev argument, so git walks HEAD only**
(`commit_impact.py:194-197`).

Through MCP, `code_root` is `config.repo_root(None)` = the container's
`REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` clone, created ONCE at container boot by
`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh:290` (`git clone --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch
main`). Nothing ever advances that clone's HEAD afterwards. The attested-gate snapshot
machinery DOES fetch (`rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.fetch_origin`), which advances
`refs/remotes/origin/main` but never HEAD or the worktree. So the referencing commit is
present in the clone's object database and reachable from `origin/main`, yet invisible to the
HEAD-only scan.

Reproduced end to end: a `--single-branch` clone, one upstream commit whose subject is
`d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231: …`, then `git fetch` in the clone. `git log` shows only the clone-time
commit; `git log --all` shows both. `referencing_commits` returns `[]` in the clone and
`['c67195b…']` in the up-to-date checkout — the same ticket, the same commit, two verdicts.

The guard already distinguishes "history unreadable" (`None` → allow) from "no commit" (`[]` →
refuse), but a checkout that reads fine and simply does not have that commit ON HEAD returns
`[]`, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely commit-less target.

## Design

Two layered corrections to `caused_by_refusal`'s evidence, neither of which weakens the guard:

1. **Scan every ref, not just HEAD.** `referencing_commits` grows an opt-in `all_refs` flag
   that appends `--all` (a strict superset of HEAD) to the `git log` argv. The `caused_by`
   guard opts in; the close gate's caller (`close_precheck._referencing_commits`) does NOT, so
   its "reachable from your worktree's current HEAD" contract is unchanged byte for byte.
2. **A negative needs a current view.** When the all-refs scan still finds nothing AND the
   checkout has a configured remote, refresh the remote-tracking refs once (bounded
   `git fetch`, serialized by the existing `fetch_coordination_lock`) and rescan. If the
   refresh fails (offline, auth, timeout) the checkout cannot be shown to hold the project's
   history, so the outcome is the SAME as the existing unreadable-history case — allow,
   because a refusal must never mean "this checkout might be missing history". A checkout with
   NO remote is the whole world, so absence there is proof and the refusal stands.

Rejected alternatives: (a) skipping the check on MCP — a silent per-surface weakening, exactly
the surface-parity defect class this project guards against; (b) pointing the MCP scan at the
tickets store — the wrong history, and `_code_root` exists precisely to avoid that; (c) a
periodic `git pull` in the MCP entrypoint — infrastructure-only, portable to no other
deployment, and it would leave every other lagging checkout broken.

## Definition of done

- DD1 - `referencing_commits` accepts `all_refs` (default `False`, argv unchanged when unset).
- DD2 - `caused_by_refusal` scans all refs, and on a miss refreshes a configured remote once
  and rescans before refusing; a failed/absent refresh degrades to allow / refuse respectively.
- DD3 - Refusal text and the `--force` remedy are unchanged for a genuinely commit-less target.
- DD4 - Tests exercise the fix through the MCP `link_tickets` tool, not only the library.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 - The mechanism is confirmed: the MCP clone's HEAD is frozen at container-boot clone
      time while the referencing commit arrives only on `origin/main`, so the HEAD-only scan
      cannot see it. (Confirmed above.)
- [x] AC2 - A `caused_by` target whose commit exists on `main` but is not on the scanning
      checkout's HEAD is NOT refused as "has no commit".
- [x] AC3 - Defect-seeded test: a link whose target is referenced by a commit absent from the
      scanning clone but present upstream must not be refused.
- [x] AC4 - A genuinely commit-less target in a complete checkout is STILL refused, with the
      same message.
- [x] AC5 - The close gate's referencing-commit scan is unchanged (still HEAD-scoped).
- [x] AC6 - The MCP `link_tickets` tool path is proven by test, not inferred from the library.

## Surfaces

Guarded by `caused_by_refusal`, all covered by the fix: the CLI write (`link_cli` →
`link_core`), the CLI `--dry-run` preview (`_link_dry_run`), the library facade (`rebar.link`),
and the MCP `link_tickets` tool (`_mcp_writes.py:407`, which calls `rebar.link`). Out of scope:
the bug-close blame link (`transition_close._apply_caused_by`) writes its LINK event directly
and never consults this guard, so it neither exhibits nor is affected by the defect.

## Portability

No CI dependency and no new configuration: the change is in-process git plumbing on the
operation's own path, so every deployment — CI, no CI, container, laptop — gets it.

## Non-goals

Not removing the `caused_by` commit guard — refusing a genuinely commit-less target is correct
and deliberate.

caused_by_refusal delegates to _absence_is_proven, with a tri-state _remote_probe: none (this checkout IS the history, refuse stands), present (bounded fetch under the existing lock, then rescan), unknown (indeterminate, allow rather than manufacture a --force-only dead end).

defect-seeded tests for the lagging-checkout refusal, proven RED against unmodified src with the exact reported refusal text; covers both directions (allow after refresh, and still-refuse for a genuinely commit-less target) through the library and through the MCP link_tickets tool.
